core.title: Pick exactly one quality lens per plan artifact
core.given: You are authoring or revising a plan artifact.
core.then: Select exactly one catalog lens value (social, functional, or emotional) most relevant to the work the plan artifact describes.
prefer: social_lens (identity/belonging drives): belong = accepted by a group, align with norms; stand_out = differentiate positively — uniqueness/status/taste/expertise; affirm = reinforce an existing identity; aspire = become a better future self.

functional_lens (task-outcome qualities): efficiency = minimize time/effort/resources; effectiveness = improve quality/accuracy/impact; availability = accessible and operational when needed; adaptability = handle new/changing requirements; sustainability = maintain performance over time.

emotional_lens (felt reactions): joy = pleasure when friction is removed; trust = confidence it is reliable and safe; fear = anxiety about a negative outcome; surprise = reaction to the unexpected; sadness = unhappiness from loss/blocked goal; disgust = aversion to unethical/cluttered design; anger = frustration when things fail; anticipation = hopeful expectation.
avoid: Several lenses on one plan artifact, or a value outside the catalog.
A lens not matched to the described work.
core.why: The method asks for the one lens most relevant to the work, so the plan artifact is framed by that quality alone.
evidence: Each plan artifact carries exactly one lens reference whose value belongs to the social, functional, or emotional catalog.
A reviewer judges the chosen lens as the most relevant to the plan artifact's statement.
verification: A structural check over plan artifacts confirms each declares exactly one lens value drawn from the lens catalog, whose three categories carry the term ids social_lens, functional_lens and emotional_lens; several lenses on one artifact, or a value outside the catalog, fail.

The check covers only presence, uniqueness and catalog membership of the lens value; whether the chosen lens is the most relevant to the described work is not mechanically decidable and is judged (reviewer/LLM) against the plan artifact's statement.

values: lens not most relevant to the work

fires: A plan author adds a new plan artifact to the plan tree.
A plan author edits an existing plan artifact's statement or its lens reference.
doesNotFire: Editing acceptance test code without touching plan artifact definitions.
Editing plan-tree metadata that contains no plan artifact entries.

neutralityNotes: The rule is method-level, not stack-mechanical: the lens catalog (social/functional/emotional, its values, and the term ids social_lens, functional_lens, emotional_lens) carries no stack content and stays verbatim in the core's then, prefer and verification — nothing in this rule is Bun-only, so bunOnly is empty. Only three things are stack facts, all delivered through the profile: the plan artifact's local name (WMBT, roles.plan_artifact.name), its concrete file kinds (wmbt plan yaml, wagon plan yaml, roles.plan_artifact.kinds), and the lens field construct (lens_ref, via the proposed idiom.plan_syntax#plan_lens_ref — no existing vocabulary key fits). 'Wagon plan' in fires/doesNotFire was generalized to 'plan tree'/'plan-tree metadata'; the obligation does not depend on the wagon notion. Whether the chosen lens is the most relevant remains llm_judged in every stack, so evidence[1] and the second verification entry keep that judgment outside the structural check.
